# Golden State Warriors 2026/27 NBA Season Preview: Whole Lotta Nothing

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-08-22, 30:29. https://youtu.be/LXZLrL90crE

## Summary

Josh Lloyd and Charlie Walter of Locked On Warriors preview the 2026/27 Golden State Warriors. They describe a thin, boring roster in what is reportedly a gap year. Jimmy Butler (ACL) is expected to miss the start of the season and Moses Moody has a serious injury. Their projected starters are Steph Curry, Brandon Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Draymond Green and Kristaps Porzingis, with lots of lineup mixing under Steve Kerr. Because the team is so thin, wing and guard players should see more minutes. Josh expects Podziemski to top 30 minutes and Lendeborg to be second in that group. Steph will carry a huge offensive load at 38, and Charlie predicts about 43 wins.

## Rules and methods

- [15:53](https://youtu.be/LXZLrL90crE?t=953) On a team with poor depth, role players' minutes go up. Players who played 22 minutes may play 26, and players who played 27 may play 31.
  > "these guys that played 22 minutes are going to have to play 26 and the guys who played 27"
- [18:48](https://youtu.be/LXZLrL90crE?t=1128) Players coming back from ACL injuries usually have their minutes managed and sit out back to backs early on.
  > "he'll be managed through and he'll play lowish minutes and he'll sit his back to backs"
- [19:12](https://youtu.be/LXZLrL90crE?t=1152) Players whose game relies on IQ and strength, not explosiveness, return from an ACL injury better than speed-based players like Zach LaVine.
  > "there is a case to be made that he'd come back and still be a very effective, highly winning player"
- [17:42](https://youtu.be/LXZLrL90crE?t=1062) Teams locked into a seed have no reason to rush injured players back late in the season.
  > "why why would you rush him back? They're pretty much locked into the 10 the entire second half"
- [29:32](https://youtu.be/LXZLrL90crE?t=1772) Injury-risk players can still hold fantasy value.
  > "Same with Porzingis, but there's still value in these guys."
